Name: PHM North America 2023 Conference Data Challenge
Summary: Vibration and tachometer signals from a gear pitting test rig at many speeds and torques, covering eleven health levels, for estimating gearbox fault severity.
Description:
The PHM North America 2023 Conference Data Challenge, hosted on the PHM Society data repository, asks teams to estimate the degradation of a gearbox run under many operating conditions, and each result must carry a measure of confidence. The data come from gear pitting experiments on a one-stage spur gearbox in an electronically closed transmission test rig with two 45 kW Siemens servo motors.

A tri-axial accelerometer near the output-end bearing house records horizontal, axial and vertical acceleration at 20480 Hz, with a tachometer signal in the last column. Gear teeth are degraded by hand with a drill bit, from level 0 (healthy) up to 10. The training set holds 2016 files from 15 rotational speeds and 6 torque levels for the healthy state and six fault levels; levels 5, 7, 9 and 10 are left out.

Test and validation data span 11 health levels, 18 speeds and 6 torque levels. Each submission gives a probability per health state and a binary confidence flag, and points depend on the distance from the true state, weighted by confidence.
